rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law – deposit cap and handling
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent, and yearly increases to the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Deposits are held in trust in an interest-bearing New Jersey account, and prepaid rent (including last month's rent) counts toward the cap. The first month's rent may also be collected, so no more than 2.5 months' rent at lease start.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent max; annual increase max 10%
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant can opt in by written request, effective 30 days later); seasonal rentals (125 days or less) exempt from the interest-bearing account section.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act – good cause for non-renewal
rules.requirement: Landlords of most residential rentals may not refuse to renew a lease, or evict a tenant just because the lease term ended, unless they have a statutory good cause. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels/hotels, and transient or seasonal units are excluded.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease
rules.key_value: good cause required to evict or not renew
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient or seasonal units.

parsed.doc_summary: Part 1 of the NJ DCA Truth in Renting guide. It supports two NJ state rules: the security deposit cap (1.5 months' rent, 10% annual increase limit) and the Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement for non-renewal. The eviction, rent control, screening and background-check sections fall in later parts.
